{{DISPLAYTITLE:Semi-''s''-cobordism}}
In [[mathematics]], a [[cobordism]] (''W'', ''M'', ''M''<sup>&minus;</sup>) of an (''n''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)-dimensional [[manifold]] (with boundary) ''W'' between its boundary components, two ''n''-manifolds ''M'' and ''M''<sup>&minus;</sup>, is called a '''semi-''s''-cobordism''' if (and only if) the inclusion <math>M \hookrightarrow W</math> is a [[Homotopy equivalence|simple homotopy equivalence]] (as in an [[s-cobordism|''s''-cobordism]]), with no further requirement on the inclusion <math>M^- \hookrightarrow W</math> (not even being a homotopy equivalence).

==Other notations==
The original creator of this topic, Jean-Claude Hausmann, used the notation ''M''<sub>&minus;</sub> for the right-hand boundary of the cobordism.

==Properties==
A consequence of (''W'', ''M'', ''M''<sup>&minus;</sup>) being a semi-''s''-cobordism is that the [[Kernel (algebra)|kernel]] of the derived [[homomorphism]] on [[fundamental group]]s <math>K = \ker(\pi_1(M^{-}) \twoheadrightarrow \pi_1(W))</math> is [[Perfect group|perfect]]. A corollary of this is that <math>\pi_1(M^{-})</math> solves the [[Group extension|group extension problem]] <math>1 \rightarrow K \rightarrow \pi_1(M^{-}) \rightarrow \pi_1(M) \rightarrow 1</math>. The solutions to the group extension problem for prescribed [[quotient group]] <math>\pi_1(M)</math> and kernel group K are classified up to congruence by group cohomology (see Mac Lane's ''Homology'' pp. 124-129), so there are restrictions on which n-manifolds can be the right-hand boundary of a semi-''s''-cobordism with prescribed left-hand boundary M and superperfect kernel group K.

==Relationship with Plus cobordisms==
Note that if (''W'', ''M'', ''M''<sup>&minus;</sup>) is a semi-''s''-cobordism, then (''W'',&nbsp;''M''<sup>&minus;</sup>,&nbsp;''M'') is a [[Plus construction|plus cobordism]]. (This justifies the use of ''M''<sup>&minus;</sup> for the right-hand boundary of a semi-''s''-cobordism, a play on the traditional use of ''M''<sup>+</sup> for the right-hand boundary of a plus cobordism.) Thus, a semi-''s''-cobordism may be thought of as an inverse to Quillen's Plus construction in the manifold category. Note that (''M''<sup>&minus;</sup>)<sup>+</sup> must be [[diffeomorphism|diffeomorphic]] (respectively, [[Piecewise linear homeomorphism|piecewise-linearly (PL) homeomorphic]]) to ''M'' but there may be a variety of choices for (''M''<sup>+</sup>)<sup>&minus;</sup> for a given closed [[Differentiable manifold|smooth]] (respectively, [[Piecewise linear manifold|PL]]) manifold ''M''.
